record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Find combinatorial conditions on a colored graph representing a PL manifold M that imply specified homotopy groups of M vanish, especially conditions forcing pi_1(M) or pi_2(M) to be trivial.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An (n+1)-colored graph is a pair (G, γ) where G is a finite multigraph (loops not allowed but multiple edges permitted) which is regular of degree n+1, and γ : E(G) → {0, 1, …, n} is an edge-coloring such that edges incident to the same vertex receive pairwise distinct colors. For each subset B ⊆ {0,…,n}, let G_B denote the subgraph of G obtained by keeping only the edges whose color lies in B; its connected components are called B-residues.

To each (n+1)-colored graph one associates an n-dimensional simplicial cell complex K(G) as follows: take an n-simplex σ_v for each vertex v of G, label the (n−1)-faces of σ_v by the colors {0,…,n}, and for each edge of G with color c joining v and w glue the c-labeled (n−1)-faces of σ_v and σ_w via the simplicial map preserving the color labels of their (n−2)-faces. The colored graph (G, γ) is said to represent a closed connected PL n-manifold M if |K(G)| is PL-homeomorphic to M; this happens iff for every color c ∈ {0,…,n}, every ({0,…,n}∖{c})-residue of G represents the standard PL (n−1)-sphere. Such (G, γ) (with K(G) having exactly n+1 vertices in the contracted case) is called a crystallization of M.

Problem. Determine purely combinatorial conditions on a colored graph (G, γ) representing a closed PL n-manifold M that imply the vanishing of specified homotopy groups π_k(M). In particular, find such combinatorial criteria on (G, γ) that force π_1(M) = 0, and, separately, criteria that force π_2(M) = 0.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on crystallization theory provides presentations of π_1(M) from a colored graph and combinatorial invariants linked to the fundamental group, but no general combinatorial criterion forcing π_1(M) = 0 or π_2(M) = 0 from the colored graph alone appears to be known. Standard surveys present this as an active research direction without a resolution.

status_evidence.title: A graph-theoretical representation of PL-manifolds — A survey on crystallizations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey covering crystallization-theoretic combinatorial invariants, including those related to the fundamental group of the represented manifold.
status_evidence.claim: Combinatorial invariants from crystallizations relate to π_1, but no general combinatorial vanishing criterion is established.

status_evidence.title: Manifold crystallization - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: A coloured graph encodes a closed PL n-manifold iff every n-residue represents the standard PL (n−1)-sphere; combinatorial presentations of π_1 are given.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational combinatorial framework exists but does not give general vanishing conditions for higher homotopy groups.
